Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 grants data subjects the right to access, request correction or deletion of their data, block access, and oppose usage for specific purposes (Section 19). The SeyID platform allows users to view their own NIN, date of birth, and ID details in the virtual card. The DPA also grants rights to data portability and rectification. Citizens can request copies of their civil registration records through CertExpress.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Seychelles has general judicial oversight through its courts, and the Data Protection Act 2023 provides rights of appeal against enforcement notices to the Commission (Section 13). The Constitution (Article 20) recognises the right to privacy. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms (such as dedicated ID ombudsman, ID appeals tribunal, or constitutional court review of ID-specific issues) have been identified in available sources.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 establishes partial data sharing rules: it sets consent requirements, data minimisation principles, purpose limitation, and cross-border transfer safeguards (Seychelles is the first African country to recognise the CBPR mechanism). The SeyID eKYC explicitly requires customer approval before sending identity data to service providers. However, a comprehensive published data-sharing framework specifically for the identity system has not been identified; the DPA's 18-month transition period runs until mid-2025.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Seychelles enacted the Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023), signed by President Ramkalawan on 19 December 2023 and published on 22 December 2023. It replaces the Data Protection Act 2003 which was never implemented in practice. The 2023 Act aligns with GDPR principles, covers rights of data subjects, creates enforcement mechanisms including fines, mandates data protection impact assessments for high-risk activities, and provides for cross-border data transfer safeguards.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 designates the Information Commission (established under the Access to Information Act) as the competent authority to enforce data protection law. The Commission has powers to conduct investigations, audits, issue enforcement notices, impose fines up to SCR 200,000, and order suspension of data flows. This constitutes an operational data protection authority with oversight of digital identity data.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Seychelles has a well-established legal framework for identity. The Civil Status Act governs civil registration and identity management (originally 1893, updated to 2022). The National Identity Number system has been compulsory by law since 1995. The Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) enacted December 2023 provides a comprehensive legal framework covering digital data processing, privacy rights, and oversight. The Minister for Finance announced in November 2022 budget that the digital ID system is legally operational.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance plays a partial oversight role. The 2022 budget speech by Finance Minister Naadir Hassan explicitly referred to the SeyID system as 'key to the Digital Economy Agenda', allocated R145.1 million in 2023 for ICT projects, and announced priorities for SeyID platform integration. The World Bank Digital Government report recommended giving DICT 'a Ministry of Finance backed power to veto spending on technology projects' — suggesting this power was not yet fully formalised. Finance oversees budgetary allocations but full formal oversight mechanism is not confirmed.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Seychelles collects both facial and fingerprint biometrics. The biometric passport introduced in November 2022 includes an electronic chip with facial recognition and fingerprint data. The SeyID eKYC process uses facial video selfie for verification. The National Population Database contains biographic and photographic data. Biometric passports are produced by IN Groupe with full biometric collection at enrollment stations.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration requiring national ID is mandatory in Seychelles. A December 2020 Seychelles Nation article describes stricter SIM registration regulations: carriers must verify and record customer personally identifiable information prior to SIM activation; unregistered SIMs were deactivated by January 2021. PikaSim (2026) confirms 'Seychelles requires national ID or passport registration for SIM cards. Carriers must maintain customer identification records under telecommunications regulations.' National ID or passport is the required document.
